Kerala Educator Reflects on Transition from Remote Tribal Teaching to School Staff Position

A Career Defined by Remote Access

For over two decades, K.R. Usha Kumari served as the sole instructor at the Agasthya Multi Grade Learning Centre, located within the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve in Kerala's Thiruvananthapuram district. Starting in 2002, her daily commute became a focal point of her service, requiring a routine that spanned several modes of transportation and rugged terrain:

  • Two-wheeler transit: A ride from her home to the Kumbikkal Kadavu riverbank.
  • River crossing: Navigating the water via a traditional wooden boat.
  • Forest trek: An eight-kilometre uphill hike through dense forest to reach the Kunnathumala settlement.

During her tenure, she was responsible for teaching students from Classes 1 through 4, managing all subjects, administrative tasks, and coordinating school meals. Despite national recognition and numerous state awards for her dedication, her position remained contractual, leading to intermittent pay and professional uncertainty.

Shift in Educational Infrastructure

In March 2022, the Kerala government initiated the closure of 271 Multi Grade Learning Centres across the state, citing a move to consolidate students into schools with broader facilities. This administrative decision affected 344 educators, including Usha Kumari, who had dedicated years to remote tribal instruction.

As part of a rehabilitation program for the displaced staff, Usha Kumari was reassigned as a sweeper at a government school in Peroorkada. She assumed this new role in June 2022.

Professional Outlook and Verification

While the transition marked a significant change in her career path—moving from the classroom to general maintenance—Usha Kumari has noted that the new position provides a necessary measure of financial stability that was often missing during her time as a contract teacher.

She has publicly advocated for the government to account for her 23 years of instructional service when determining her pension and seniority status. Interested readers can verify the details of the state’s education policy changes and the status of the former Multi Grade Learning Centres by consulting official government education department reports from Kerala and archived state educational records.
